---
title: "pyspatialuncertainty"
subtitle: "Uncertainty of spatial averages and totals of maps"
---

Many maps of natural resources are aggregated into averages or totals over regions:
carbon stocks per country, mean soil organic carbon per department, forest area per
district. Once a map comes with point-level uncertainty, the uncertainty of those
aggregates **depends strongly on how the map errors are correlated in space**. Averaging
the point standard deviations overstates it. Treating the errors as independent
understates it, more and more as the region grows.

`pyspatialuncertainty` implements the Monte Carlo method of
[Wadoux & Heuvelink (2023)](https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.14106). It works for maps
made with any method, including machine learning, as long as the method provides
point-level predictive distributions. For a block *B* it estimates

$$
\operatorname{var}\Big(\frac{1}{|B|}\int_B \varepsilon(s)\,ds\Big)
 = \frac{1}{|B|^2}\int_B\int_B \sigma(s)\,\sigma(u)\,\rho(|s-u|)\,ds\,du
$$

by Monte Carlo integration, where:

- σ is the point-support prediction-error standard deviation;
- ρ is the correlation function of the standardized prediction errors, fitted to
  cross-validation or independent validation errors.

It also provides a per-class analogue for maps of calibrated class probabilities. That
mode gives the uncertainty of expected class fractions and class areas.

## Installation

The package needs Python ≥ 3.12. It is not on PyPI; install the 1.0.0 release straight
from GitHub:

```bash
uv add "pyspatialuncertainty @ git+https://github.com/GMoncrieff/pyspatialuncertainty@v1.0.0"
# or: pip install "git+https://github.com/GMoncrieff/pyspatialuncertainty@v1.0.0"
```

Add the `ml` extra (`pyspatialuncertainty[ml] @ git+...`) for the synthetic QRF pipeline.
To work on the package itself, clone it:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/GMoncrieff/pyspatialuncertainty
cd pyspatialuncertainty
uv sync
```

## Quick start

```{python}
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
import xarray as xr
import pyspatialuncertainty as psu

# A 60 x 60 map of predictions and point-support prediction-error SDs (step 2)
x = np.arange(60) + 0.5
coords = {"y": x[::-1], "x": x}
pred = xr.DataArray(10 + 0.1 * np.add.outer(x[::-1], x), coords=coords, dims=("y", "x"))
sd = xr.DataArray(1 + 0.5 * np.sin(np.add.outer(x[::-1], x) / 20), coords=coords, dims=("y", "x"))

# Standardized validation errors (step 3) and a model of their correlation (step 4).
# Here the model is set by hand; in practice: model = psu.fit_correlation(val).model
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
val = pl.DataFrame({"x": rng.uniform(0, 60, 300), "y": rng.uniform(0, 60, 300),
                    "std_error": rng.normal(size=300)})
model = psu.vgm(0.6, "Exp", 5.0, nugget=0.4)

# Steps 5-8 for 20 x 20 tiles
res = psu.aggregate_continuous(sd, model, psu.blocks.tiles(sd, 20), prediction=pred, seed=1)
res.table.select("block_id", "mean_pred", "sd_mean", "lower", "upper", "sd_total")
```
